title: Closed-system mass conservation
process: volume exchange in a closed system: tanks joined by a pipe (SWMM); a closed basin (CPU surface solver)
equations: tank volume V = A d (prismatic: SWMM STORAGE FUNCTIONAL 0 0 A)
full conduit volume = (pi D^2 / 4) L; part-full conduit volume in motion is not determined by the outputs (estimate L A(y), bracket L A(min end depth) .. L A(max end depth))
at rest (one level h everywhere): V0 = sum A_i h + L A(h), solved for h
initialConditions: C1-a, C1-c: tanks at 3.0 and 2.0 m (pipe crown 0.5 m: full). C1-b: 0.45 and 0.05 m (pipe part full). The conduit starts at the mean of its end depths, capped at full: SWMM's stated initial condition (flowrout.c initLinkDepths), adopted as an input. C1-d: a Gaussian mound h = 0.5 exp(-r^2 / 25) m centred in the basin, at rest.
boundaryConditions: none: no inflow, outflow, evaporation or seepage (CPU: walls on all four sides). SWMM needs an outfall (ERROR 145 without one): it is reached only over a weir from T2 with its crest 4.5 m above the tank floor, above any level the tanks can reach (3.0 m at most), and the weir's flow is a scored row that must be zero. C1-c: an orifice between the tanks, held shut by a control rule until 1 h, then open.

definitionRevisions.why: after the criteria were registered, before any scored run: the sealing weir and outfall added, because SWMM would not open the network without an outfall. Criteria unchanged (same hash).

geometry: two 100 m^2 tanks, inverts 0, 5 m deep; one circular conduit D 0.5 m, L 50 m, inverts 0 at both ends. C1-c adds a 0.3 x 0.5 m side orifice at invert 0. C1-d: 40 x 40 cells of 1 m, bed a bowl z = 0.001 r^2 (r from the centre), Manning n 0.03.

cpuBasin.unit: cells, m, m^-1, s m^-1/3, m, s, steps

solver: SWMM 5.2.4 (vendor/swmm-wasm) dynamic wave, EXTRAN surcharge, fixed 1 s step, inertial damping PARTIAL; CPU surface solver (src/solver-cpu.js) defaults: MUSCL minmod, HLLC, SSP-RK2, CFL 0.48

reference.sources: conservation of volume; prismatic geometry; circular segment area (references/geometry.mjs)
reference.independence: the reference volume V0 is computed from the inputs alone; the simulated volumes from simulated depths and the reference geometry, never from the solver's own volume. SWMM's node volumes and continuity report are kept beside them as separate accounting rows.
reference.crossCheck: refs.test.mjs: segment area by quadrature; the bracket contains the linear-surface integral; the equilibrium round trip

outputs: SWMM node volume against A d
criteriaNotes: 0.1 % is tighter than Gate C's 0.5 % on purpose: a closed system has no throughput to hide error in. 1e-6 for the fp64 CPU solver, whose draining-time limiter claims exact mass. At rest means: the two levels within 1 mm, and level change within 1 mm over the last hour.
resolution: SWMM: one conduit, 1 s step; CPU: 1 m cells, CFL step
assumptions: the conduit's initial depth is SWMM's stated convention (the mean of its end depths), taken as an input
a part-full conduit's water surface between its ends is monotone (for the bracket)
limitations: SWMM 5.2.4 exposes no conduit volume (no LINK_VOLUME): in motion, a part-full conduit's volume is an estimate; where its bracket exceeds the criterion the row is Insufficient reference data, not a pass
C1-d checks the CPU implementation of the surface scheme, not the production GPU path
validRange: closed systems at rest at the end of the run; conduit full throughout (C1-a, C1-c) for in-motion closure
scoring: automated: lib/score.mjs row(); statuses never merged

criteriaRevisions.why: first registration, before the first run
